title: Whether the Home Caregiving Grant can cover people needing help with two daily activities
asked: Mr Kwek asked whether the Government will consider extending the Home Caregiving Grant to families caring for persons who need assistance with two, instead of three, activities of daily living, especially where the care recipient's ability to live independently is significantly impaired.
response: Mr Tan said there is a range of care schemes, including the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund, Migrant Domestic Worker Levy Concession and subsidised home- or centre-based care. The Home Caregiving Grant is targeted at those with higher functional impairment who need permanent help with at least three of six activities of daily living. He said the three-ADL threshold is applied consistently and fairly, while individual circumstances are considered for other care and caregiver support schemes not tied to the ADL threshold, such as enhanced Home Personal Care, Interim Caregiver Support, SMF and Nursing Home Respite Care.
